audit.why: 51.47% over 1193 games with Akshan on every packet row. He has no escape and no lockdown until Event Horizon at 20s rank 1; Akshan can leave any trade. EVEN 5.5/10 with a 6/10 carry threat is right, because Veigar's scaling is real even when the lane is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[] gave Veigar the first-item and 2+ item rows while win[] and the packet give both to Akshan.
audit.why: Veigar's spike is Phenomenal Evil stacking, which is a threat you deny by shoving him off Baleful Strike, not a row he wins in this data.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side flipped to Akshan with ratings realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primordial Burst is called a global execute in three fields, and Akshan is given an 'E-stun'.
audit.why: Primordial Burst is 650 range and only scales on missing health — it is not global, and Comeuppance at 2500 simply out-reaches it. Heroic Swing has no crowd control whatsoever. Event Horizon stuns only on its edge, is 725 range and 20s at rank 1, and its radius is large, not tiny. Baleful Strike is a 6s poke at 1000 range; Dark Matter has no fixed cooldown of its own and gets faster as Phenomenal Evil stacks, which is why denying his stacks is the real lane job.
audit.corrected: Global claim removed from whys[4], mid and spikes[1]; the fabricated stun removed from spikes[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers, and the single most punishable one is enormous.
audit.why: Event Horizon at 20s rank 1 is the longest lane cooldown in this matchup — a whiffed cage is a twenty-second free window.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why is garbled placeholder text naming Akshan's ultimate 'Vengeance'; wants.you[2] tells you to snowball Baleful Strike stacks, which are Veigar's stacks.
audit.why: Akshan gains nothing from Baleful Strike; the play is denying the last-hits that feed it.

edits.before: Avengerang... no — R online: Vengeance executes the chipped from two screens. Chip, then channel.
edits.after: Both ults at 6: Comeuppance reaches 2500, Primordial Burst only 650. Chip, then channel.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Heroic Swing for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Only the cage EDGE stuns — stand near its centre or leave before it forms, and never swing into the wall. - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1, the longest cooldown in this lane: a whiffed cage buys you twenty seconds against a man whose only other spell is a 6s poke.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the cage edge and executing you with a Primordial Burst that scales on missing health.

edits.before: Carry through strings and executes — chip everything, finish anything under a third, and let the swing write angles no one wards.
edits.after: Carry from outside 725: the cage cannot reach you there, and Comeuppance answers his 650-range ultimate from 2500 away.

edits.before: If Veigar takes first blood, tighten up: Event Horizon (Cage) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q strings and stay relevant through R executes.
edits.after: If Veigar takes first blood, remember Phenomenal Evil is permanent — deny every Baleful Strike last-hit and never stand on a cage edge. A second kill means the duel is over: farm from 850 and chip toward Comeuppance.

edits.before: Ahead, bully harder: string Veigar off every contact, swing-roam the rivers, and execute the map's mistakes with R.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the stacks: deny his Baleful Strike kills, shove him under tower, and Comeuppance him when he steps out.

edits.before: Bully the contact points — your string trades beat almost everything mid at level 1-3. Bank the lane lead before assassin timers start.
edits.after: Bully the contact points: he has no lockdown until level 3 and no escape at all, so every Baleful Strike he walks up for costs him health.

edits.before: Comeuppance counters his global execute ultimate, giving you the edge at level 6.
edits.after: Primordial Burst is only 650 range, so Comeuppance out-reaches it at 2500.

edits.before: Comeuppance is a hard answer to his Primordial Burst — if he ults a low-HP ally across the map you can R in to zone the kill, and his own Baleful Strike stacking means he's rarely tanky enough to punish the dive back.
edits.after: Comeuppance answers Primordial Burst on range alone — his reaches 650 and yours 2500, so you can chip him from outside his kill range entirely, and all those Baleful Strike stacks never made him tanky enough to punish you back.

edits.before: Once you have lethality or a dash-enabling item, Event Horizon's tiny cage radius stops mattering — you W-camo in, bait the cage on a decoy angle, then E-stun through it before he can flash away.
edits.after: Once you have a lethality item, one bad Event Horizon ends him — W-camo in, bait the cage on a decoy angle, then swing past its edge and string three hits before those 20 seconds are up.

edits.before: Comeuppance directly answers his global Primordial Burst executes, letting you race in and either save the kill or trade his ult for nothing. He needs to land Event Horizon to cage you before he can safely all-in, and your mobility from E and W makes that cage a low-percentage bet — most Veigars will play passive and farm rather than risk the engage.
edits.after: Comeuppance out-ranges his 650-unit Primordial Burst by nearly four times, so you chip him and execute from outside the range he needs to kill you at all. He still has to land Event Horizon before he can safely all-in, and at 20s on rank 1 that cage is a low-percentage bet — most Veigars will play passive and farm rather than risk the engage.

edits.before: Snowball Baleful Strike stacks against him early
edits.after: Deny his Baleful Strike last-hits with Avengerang
